issues.legal_issue: A court-issued certificate recording an already completed judicial auction transfer is not an instrument of sale that attracts municipal transfer duty.
material_facts: The property was purchased at an auction sale held in execution of a civil decree.
The sale was confirmed before the court issued a certificate of sale.
Title passed by operation of law when the sale became final; the certificate recorded the completed transfer and identified the property, purchaser, and date of finality.
The lower courts held that municipal transfer duty was not payable on the certificate, and the appeal challenged that result.
issues.conclusion: The certificate of sale was not an instrument of sale attracting duty under section 147 of the Delhi Municipal Corporation Act, 1957. The appeal was dismissed; the certificate remained subject to stamp duty under the Indian Stamp Act, 1899, without the municipal surcharge.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 147 of the Delhi Municipal Corporation Act, 1957, an instrument of sale is a document that effects the transfer of title, not one that merely records a transfer already completed. Under Order XXI, Rules 92 and 94 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, title to property sold in execution passes when the sale becomes final upon confirmation; the certificate formally records that effect and does not create or extinguish title. The judgment cites no earlier cases for this principle.

rule.if: civil_execution_auction_sale and sale_confirmed_before_certificate and title_passed_before_certificate and certificate_only_records_completed_transfer

predicates.civil_execution_auction_sale: The proceeding concerns an immovable property auction conducted to enforce a civil decree.
predicates.sale_confirmed_before_certificate: The court confirmed the auction sale before issuing the certificate.
predicates.title_passed_before_certificate: The purchaser's title passed before the certificate was issued.
predicates.certificate_only_records_completed_trans: The court-issued certificate recorded a transfer that had already become final rather than effecting the transfer.

issues.definition: When an immovable property is sold in execution of a civil decree, the sale is confirmed before a certificate is issued, title has already passed, and the certificate only records that transfer, the certificate is not subject to municipal transfer duty.
